state.misconception_label: Does not know the properties of a rectangle

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: The angles highlighted on this rectangle with different length sides can never be... ![A rectangle with the diagonals drawn in. The angle on the right hand side at the centre is highlighted in red and the angle at the bottom at the centre is highlighted in yellow.](). I got acute because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you were building a rectangular table with different length sides. Would all the angles in the table be equal?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, no - the corners of the table would all be 90 degrees, but the angles in the middle where the diagonals cross would be different. So I was wrong about all the angles being equal... but I'm still not sure what those angles in the middle can never be?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you were playing a game of tic-tac-toe on a rectangular board. Would all the angles at the center where the lines cross be the same?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher uses real-world analogies but doesn't directly address the diagonal properties of rectangles, and by Turn 3 repeats a similar question despite the student already correcting their initial misconception and asking a more specific question about what the center angles can never be.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses concrete, everyday analogies (building a rectangular table, playing tic-tac-toe) to help the student visualize and understand the abstract geometric properties of angles in a rectangle with diagonals.
